transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2026-03-21 15:00 PT
Duration: 63 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Samir (AE), Lina (SE), Diego (Product) — Aurora: Mark (CTO), Priya (ML), Ethan (Platform), Jenna (PM)
Links shared: https://redwood.ai/deck/aurora-demo, spreadsheet: https://docs.google.com/spreadsheets/aurora-bench, security: https://redwood.ai/security/soc2

Summary (auto): Quick demo of JSON mode / structured output and function/tool calling. Walked through Console + API flows, Optimize suggestions for batching & quantization, discussed VPC and KMS, agreed on pilot and next steps.

Topics: API structured output, JSON schemas, tool calling/fallbacks, streaming, Console Optimize suggestions, pilot & security requirements.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Samir (AE): hey everyone thanks for joining, quick roll call?
[00:08] Mark (CTO): hey Mark here, Priya and Ethan and Jenna are on as well.
[00:12] Samir: awesome, so today Lina will demo JSON mode, function calling, and we'll show some Optimize recs for cost/latency. we'll keep it practical, not a deep infra session yet, though Diego can answer product questions.
[00:28] Lina (SE): hi all, jumping in — quick context, Aurora mentioned wanting consistent structured outputs for their extract pipeline and the ability to safely call internal tools without leaking. is that still the priority?
[00:38] Priya (ML): yes, particularly the schema enforcement and predictable latency, we've been hitting a lot of post-processing fixes because models return inconsistent keys.
[00:47] Ethan (Platform): and we need the option for hosted but also private — the compliance team will want VPC and KMS.
[00:54] Samir: totally, we built the console flows to cover both. today we'll show hosted API JSON mode, then Console's schema editor, then how function/tool calling ties into runbook actions and fallbacks.
[01:12] Lina: first, quick demo — opening the Console, so on the left nav Model Playground -> JSON Mode. you can paste a JSON Schema, pin required fields, and enable validation. note: sometimes the auto-formatter shows unexpected escapes, ignore that, it's cosmetic in the browser.
[01:30] [screen share noise] Lina: ok I pasted the invoice extraction schema — sample output includes invoice_number, total_amount, currency, vendor.name, vendor.tax_id. i'm going to toggle "strict schema" which enforces types and required keys server-side.
[01:47] Jenna (PM): when you say server-side enforcement, does that mean we get a 4xx or a 200 with an error payload?
[01:54] Lina: good q — currently we return 200 with a structured validation result object alongside the response, so you get the model output and a schema_validation block. if strict mode is set to block, the platform can reject the response and trigger a fallback path. note: some customers prefer soft enforcement so they can log mismatches.
[02:12] Priya: is the validation synchronous? would that add to latency?
[02:16] Lina: validation is lightweight JSON schema validation, typically sub-ms unless you've got huge objects. the bigger latencies are model tokens; Optimize can recommend batching/quantization to reduce that.
[02:26] Mark: can you show the API call too? how we'd call it from pipeline?
[02:29] Lina: sure — here's a POST to /v1/generate with body {"mode":"json","schema_id":"invoice-v2","input":"..."}, and you can set "response.strict":true,"fallback.policy":"call_tool".
[02:42] [cough] Ethan: call_tool, what's that hook into?
[02:45] Lina: great lead-in — function/tool calling is pluggable. you register tools (webhook endpoints or internal plugins). the runtime can call the tool when the model emits a special function call object or when validation fails and the fallback route is configured.
[02:58] Diego (Product): we also have an off-ramp to a lighter model variant if latency spikes, that autopromotes a cheaper quantized model for throughput bursts.
[03:07] Priya: any risk of data leakage when calling tools? our tools talk to internal APIs with PII.
[03:13] Samir: yes good point. we support per-call data redaction and field-level encryption via KMS. for Private/VPC deployments the tool endpoints can stay inside the customer's network — the control plane just orchestrates.
[03:24] Mark: can you give an example of a tool call flow?
[03:27] Lina: sure, I'll simulate it: model returns {"function_call":{"name":"lookup_vat","args":{"vendor_name":"Acme Ltd"}}} then Redwood's runtime calls your registered endpoint /tools/lookup_vat with the args, gets back {"vat":"GB1234"}, and merges into the final JSON output. you can set permissions so only certain tools are callable by model outputs to avoid misuses.
[03:49] [teasing noise from background] Jenna: sounds neat. what about retries? if the tool times out do you expose that to the client?
[03:55] Lina: there are retries and circuit breakers — you can configure retry count and backoff. if the tool ultimately fails, fallback path options are: return partial response with error flags, retry with a non-tool fallback, call a secondary tool, or route to a human-in-the-loop queue.
[04:11] Priya: human-in-loop would be useful while we ramp. is that built-in?
[04:15] Diego: we have a simple HIL queue integration that can post to Slack, Jira, or your ticketing system with the offending payload and suggested corrections.
[04:24] [05:00] Samir: switching gears to Optimize — Lina can show how the platform suggests batching and quant profiles for our workload.
[05:05] Lina: in Console -> Optimize we ingested some sample trace (we used the spreadsheet link). Optimize suggests batch size 8 for p50 latencies under 150ms on dedicated pools, or quantize to int8 + recommended KV cache settings to reduce token compute by ~22% for the same quality threshold. note: quantization tradeoffs depend on model architecture.
[05:30] Priya: did you run evals to confirm quality regression?
[05:33] Lina: yes we ran a small eval set — there's an eval tab that ties prompt sets to regression alerts. you can set a quality delta threshold, if it trips we block automated rollouts.
[05:44] Mark: what about streaming? we need partial results for UX.
[05:47] Lina: JSON mode supports streaming tokens but also supports incremental JSON patches — you can stream fields as they become stable. remember to keep idempotency keys for retries.
[05:58] Ethan: how do we debug when the model outputs stray keys? logs?
[06:02] Lina: Console trace shows token-level timeline, and the per-request detail includes schema validation reasons. there's also a token cost breakdown and a trace link you can share with your engineers.
[06:12] [06:30] Priya: what's the dev experience for adding new tools? need to open tickets?
[06:34] Lina: developer API — you register a tool with name, schema for args, and a webhook url. you can also deploy a small adapter inside your VPC that proxies calls and enforces auth. we provide a reference adapter repo.
[06:45] Samir: quick note on security: we support SAML SSO, RBAC roles in Console, audit logs, and KMS integration for field-level encryption. Diego will send the SOC2 + KMS doc.
[06:57] Diego: yep will share, and for Private we can include HSM/KMS details.
[07:02] Jenna: timeline question — if we run a pilot in April, what would success look like for us?
[07:07] Samir: good qs — typical pilot is 2-4 weeks: 1) integrate sample tool registry + schema, 2) run benchmark with 1k inference/day, 3) evaluate regression and latency, 4) agree on SLOs. success = >=95% schema passrate and p95 latency under your target, plus cost per inference within projected range.
[07:27] Priya: what's the SLA for hosted vs dedicated?
[07:30] Samir: hosted has a 99.5% uptime target; Dedicated comes with SLA options (99.9%+ depending on contract). Private is negotiated.
[07:40] Mark: any known limitations re: extremely nested schemas?
[07:43] Lina: very deep nesting is fine but validation/comparison can increase CPU; recommend flattening heavy arrays or chunking into separate calls. also be mindful of token counts if you include large documents in the prompt.
[07:56] Ethan: can we control fallback policy by endpoint/route? we want different behavior for realtime credit checks vs batch processing.
[08:02] Lina: yes per-route policies. you can configure route_policies in the API key settings: e.g., realtime route -> strict block + secondary model fallback; batch route -> soft validation + log for human review.
[08:19] [08:30] Priya: curious about costs — can Optimize give an estimate for cost delta if we switch to int8?
[08:35] Lina: it shows estimated token compute and cost projection per 10k requests for candidate configs. it's conservative, we provide a confidence band.
[08:44] Mark: competitor question — how is this different from using a self-hosted LLM + custom middleware?
[08:49] Samir: main differences: we provide a unified runtime that handles batching, KV cache, schema validation, tool orchestration, and provides product-level guardrails (rollouts, alerts, traces). building that in-house is possible but tends to become expensive and brittle. we also maintain model compatibility and optimized kernels for common architectures.
[09:07] Jenna: any examples of customers using function calls for financial lookups?
[09:11] Lina: yes a fintech customer uses function calling to hit KYC APIs and fallback to manual verification; they set strict schema so if the model misses required fields it automatically spawns a manual review ticket.
[09:25] [09:30] Priya: do you support typed function args? like enforce enum for country codes?
[09:34] Lina: yes, you can specify arg schemas with enums, patterns, and Redwood will validate before calling the tool. you can also use that to avoid unnecessary external calls, the runtime can short-circuit if args fail validation.
[09:48] Ethan: about on-prem — how heavy is the private control plane? we have air-gapped requirements for one product line.
[09:55] Diego: we have an on-prem package used by customers with air-gap needs. it ships as an appliance image plus CLI install, and we collaborate on network egress rules. support package depends on contract.
[10:08] Mark: great — let's talk errors: a model returns an unexpected field that passes validation because it's optional, and downstream ETL breaks. how do we prevent?
[10:16] Lina: couple of patterns: 1) use strict schemas where optional fields are pruned unless whitelisted; 2) set schema_transform rules to rename/mask fields; 3) Console has regression alerts on schema diffs — if a new key appears above threshold, alert and block rollout.
[10:35] Priya: thinking about rollout safety — can we do canary rollouts of schema changes?
[10:39] Samir: yes, rollouts support canary %, A/B, and automatic rollback if quality metrics degrade. you configure evaluation prompts and metrics.
[10:48] Jenna: for the pilot we want a path: run hosted test, then move to dedicated if latency/cost warrants, then private later. is that path supported?
[10:57] Samir: absolutely — routing policies allow traffic to shift across hosted/dedicated/private with the same API and model pins.
[11:05] [11:30] Priya: quick nit — in the schema example vendor.tax_id, do you support multiple tax id formats? we have EU, US, AU.
[11:34] Lina: you can use oneOf in JSON Schema to accept multiple formats, or normalize using function calls that run a validator per country.
[11:44] Ethan: performance question — if we enable streaming + tool calls, does that add coordination overhead?
[11:49] Lina: marginally yes, because runtime needs to orchestrate streams and tool webhooks, but latency impact is small compared to model token generation. Optimize can surface expected p50/p95 deltas if you enable both.
[12:02] Mark: any pitfalls with large tool arg payloads?
[12:06] Lina: keep tool args small; if you need full docs, pass a document id and have tool fetch from your internal doc store. we also support signed short-lived URLs for secure fetches.
[12:17] Samir: going to demo one end-to-end quick flow: create schema -> set route policy -> register tool -> run sample request.
[12:24] [screen share audible keyboard sounds] Lina: creating schema, naming invoice-v2, toggling strict, saving. registering tool: lookup_vat -> webhook url placeholder -> arg schema -> save. invoking generate with sample input...
[12:42] Systems: [noise] Model returns function_call for lookup_vat -> runtime posts to registered webhook -> returns vat -> final JSON constructed.
[12:52] Priya: looks clean. can we see logs for that request?
[12:55] Lina: clicking request trace, here's token timeline, schema validation node shows success. note: if strict was block we would have triggered fallback.
[13:05] Jenna: about observability, does Console keep request bodies longer for debug? retention?
[13:10] Diego: retention depends on plan; debug traces can be retained for 30/90/365 days depending on contract and we can redact PII on ingest.
[13:20] Mark: how do we test quality drift over time?
[13:24] Lina: set up eval sets and baseline metrics, and enable regression alerts; also can run scheduled evals daily/weekly.
[13:34] Priya: when switching quant modes, do you support AB testing between quant levels?
[13:38] Lina: yes, you can AB quantized vs float models and tie metrics to traffic buckets, and automatic rollbacks exist.
[13:46] [14:00] Ethan: one more on governance — RBAC granularity? we want engineers to deploy schemas but only security can allow KMS keys.
[14:06] Diego: we support role-based permissions down to schema edit, tool register, and key bindings. you can enforce approvals for key linking.
[14:16] Samir: ok let's finalize pilot scope and next steps — we propose 2 weeks hosted test with sample schema + tool adapter, then bench, then decide Dedicated.
[14:29] Priya: sounds good. can you send the sample schema templates?
[14:32] Lina: yes will attach in follow-up.
[14:35] Mark: any costs for pilot?
[14:38] Samir: pilot is typically discounted, we can include a small flat fee for dedicated bench if you need dedicated nodes for testing. I'll send pricing options.
[14:46] Jenna: thanks all very helpful.
[14:50] [crosstalk] Samir: quick recap — I'll send deck + pricing + schema samples; Lina will push sample schemas and runner script; Diego will send security docs. Priya you'll share example prompts and success criteria. agreed?
[14:59] Priya: agreed.
[15:02] Mark: agreed.
[15:05] Samir: great, we can book tech deep dive for private next week, I'll follow up with a Doodle. thanks everyone.

End of transcript.
